text:
mike: FYI — julia-cs forwarded an ACME ticket: embeddings endpoint /v1/embeddings showing tail latency spikes (~2–8s) and intermittent 400s. ticket 12345. attaching notes below.

support-eng: copying. do we have a short repro or request samples? route + model?

mike: route=/v1/embeddings model=embed-large-prod. customer reports most requests are small (2–6 docs) sent rapidly in a loop. saw lots of 400s and tail spikes in support logs. pasted proxy/log snippets: 
```
[proxy] time=1715000012 req_id=abc123 client=1.2.3.4 path=/v1/embeddings headers={Authorization: Bearer ****, Transfer-Encoding: chunked}
body-fragment: '{"input":["doc1","doc2"],"model":"embed-large-prod"}'
error: EOF while reading body -> 400 invalid_json
batcher: early_flush trigger=chunked_body reqs_in_batch=3 max_batch_size=16
```

ana: can you paste raw headers from the ingress? chunked + short gaps could look like end-of-stream to us.

ingrid: early_flush? our batcher flushes if it sees client EOF or a client abort. if several clients are chunking small bodies with micro-gaps, the batcher may treat them as finished and flush small batches, which amplifies per-request overhead and causes tail variance.

ana: do we know sdk version? older SDKs had an http/1.1 chunking keepalive issue behind some proxies.

mike: ACME on python-sdk v1.2.3 pinned. they do HTTP/1.1 chunked transfer. proxy shows many "received small chunk; scheduling flush" log lines.

support-eng: seen that before — advise customer to try latest SDK or set Content-Length explicitly.

ingrid: also check the dynamic batching config for embed pool. current: embed-pool-5 max_batch_size=16 max_batch_latency_ms=10 dynamic=true. 10ms is pretty aggressive for chunked traffic.

ana: yep — 10ms can cause lots of small batches when chunking is noisy. suggestion: bump max_batch_latency_ms to 50ms and consider max_batch_size=32; enable prefix cache to reduce token work per batch.

mike: pushed a canary config to embed-pool-5: max_batch_latency_ms=50 (in canary).

sre-bot: deploy: config update embed-pool-5 by mike at 1715000200. status: success.

mike: after canary -> customer reports tail dropped from ~3s to ~400ms. but sporadic 400s still happening (~1/hr).

ana: the 400s are likely from client aborts mid-body: proxy logs show 'EOF while reading body' which is a client-side close. did ACME provide tcpdump?

support-eng: they did — tcpdump excerpt shows FIN mid-body on ~1% of requests during busy loops. looks like client process terminates or reuses connection poorly under high concurrency.

ingrid: two linked issues: (1) client abort -> server returns 400; (2) those aborts cause early_flush -> lots of small batches -> tail spikes. server-side mitigation: add a small tolerance window for chunked EOF (e.g., chunked_eof_wait_ms=20) to avoid immediate flush on micro-gaps. risk: adds latency for chunked requests, but chunked usage here is rare and the benefit is lower tail variance. gate behind runtime flag.

an a: agree — runtime flag per pool. canary with chunked_eof_wait_ms=20 on embed-pool-5. also request ACME to upgrade SDK to 1.3.0 and prefer HTTP/2 or explicit Content-Length.

mike: action items logged on ticket: 1) ask ACME to upgrade SDK + repro tcpdump; 2) enable chunked_eof_wait_ms=20 on embed-pool-5 as canary; 3) monitor 400-rate + tail latency for 24h. I've added notes and set watchers.

support-eng: will message ACME with repro steps + tcpdump instructions. attaching minimal tcpdump instructions: 
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w client-out.pcap host <our-proxy-ip>
# collect ~1 minute under repro load, then upload
```

mike: update: ACME upgraded to sdk v1.3.0 and we enabled canary wait=20ms. their 400/hr dropped to ~2/hr and tail latencies stabilized. marking ticket resolved and creating KB entry for chunked+batching troubleshooting.

support-eng: :thumbsup: I'll draft KB and include common mitigations (upgrade SDK, explicit content-length, bump batch latency, chunked_eof_wait_ms runtime flag).

mike: closing loop. thanks all.
